messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a 'safety lattice' for precision selection + an adaptive backoff policy. Idea: runtime picks a lattice node (fp8 -> int8 -> 4bit) and backs off to a parent node when quality/telemetry crosses thresholds. Looking for concerns around API surface, cache semantics, and telemetry.

sam: Like it. Two immediate asks: (1) make the lattice explicit in the quant/profile schema, (2) add hysteresis + tunable thresholds so we don't oscillate. :+1:

leo: Runtime implications: need per-request negotiation path and an `abort_on_fallback` flag. Also, we must avoid reusing KV cache blobs across differing precisions — that will cause silent corruption. Cache keys need to include precision bitwidth and profile id, e.g.: `cache_key = f"{model}:{profile_id}:{precision}:{input_hash}"`.

julia: Telemetry piece: propose we emit these metrics per lattice node + profile_id: `model_loss`, `sample_count`, `fallback_count`, `avg_latency_ms`, `degradation_score`. Also tag by `endpoint` and `canary_id`.

sam: Another signal: runtime should accept a `degradation_score` input from shadow evals. Policy can be "backoff when degradation_score > X for Y samples". Keeps decisions data-driven.

maria: Question for product/ops: do we expose the backoff policy to customers? My gut: expose a simple `safety_mode` enum (strict|managed|permissive). Strict = no lowbit unless explicitly pinned in profile. Managed = runtime can backoff based on lattice + telemetry. Permissive = allow lowest bitpaths unless manually disabled. Thoughts?

leo: Ops concern: exposing too many knobs will confuse teams. Recommend we ship 3 global modes + per-endpoint overrides (metadata). Keep UI/SDK ergonomics simple.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary report for `staging-nlp-3`: fp8 shadowed since 08:00 UTC — fallback_rate=2.3% (24h), avg_latency +3ms, sample_count=12.

julia: If fallback_rate > 1% we should trigger an alert. Suggest playbook entry: `if fallback_rate>1% AND avg_degradation_score>0.01 -> auto-rollback` (and create a pager policy for repeated regressions).

maria: Action items I will track: (1) schema PR to add `precision_lattice` + thresholds (assign to @sam), (2) runtime change: include precision in cache keys + backoff hook (assign @leo), (3) telemetry: implement per-node metrics + alerting (assign @julia), (4) UX decision: expose `safety_mode` with 3 options + per-endpoint override (product to finalize). I'll open issues and link this thread.

sam: :thumbsup: I can start the schema PR. Naming: `precision_lattice` vs `quant_lattice`? Any preference?

maria: Let's go with `precision_lattice` (snake_case) and keep config compact. Example snippet to include in PR:```json
{"precision_lattice": [
  {"node_id": "fp8_a", "precision": "fp8", "thresholds": {"degradation_score": 0.005, "min_samples": 100}},
  {"node_id": "int8_a", "precision": "int8", "thresholds": {"degradation_score": 0.02, "min_samples": 50}},
  {"node_id": "4bit_a", "precision": "4bit", "thresholds": {"degradation_score": 0.05, "min_samples": 25}}
]
}
``` Keep the schema minimal at first; we can iterate on policy DSL later.

leo: One more runtime note: ensure backoff decisions are idempotent and that we persist last-successful-precision per session to avoid thrashing. Also add a small TTL before allowing promotion back to lower bitwidth.

maria: Great. If nobody objects I'll open the RFC follow-up issue and tag owners. We'll aim to land the schema PR this sprint and a telemetry prototype on staging. Thanks all.
